scope: Opt-in hosted Linux and Windows build and focused headless probe for the pinned downstream FreeCAD importer candidate.
environment: FreeCAD upstream Pixi release presets, upstream-pinned setup-pixi action and Pixi version, locked environment
checks: Existing push-triggered release qualification jobs remain enabled; candidate matrix is opt-in for dispatch.
Candidate source application and headless runtime guards were separately exercised on macOS.
limitations: Two hosted candidate runs failed before build; the explicit line-ending fix has not yet been tested on hosted platforms and neither platform is qualified.
Submodule gitlink status is recorded; binary reproducibility, full build provenance and independent semantic support are not established.
Headless checks do not establish native GUI rendering or complete DWG/DXF support.
The downstream FreeCAD patch series remains unmerged.

firstDispatch.outcome: Both OS jobs failed in source replay before build. The application helper captured the underlying error and did not expose it, so its cause is not established.

followupChecks: The application helper now includes replay stderr on failure; a wrong archive produces its specific hash-mismatch diagnostic.
CMakeCache source identity rejects a candidate source paired with a different build; the matching macOS source/build passes all ten headless tests.
actionlint and Python syntax checks pass.
The public codeload archive downloaded locally matched the previously pinned SHA-256; the hosted download hash was not recorded by the first dispatch.

With global and system Git config disabled, the previous replay failed at the same second patch. Explicit core.autocrlf=input now makes replay and clean-worktree application pass with exact expected output hashes.
With global and system Git config disabled, injected fifth-patch failure restored the original bytes and a clean retry passed.

secondDispatch.outcome: Both OS jobs failed applying the second patch to dxf.h during archive replay. The archive hash check had passed.

rootCause: The archive header contains CRLF; the ordered patches depend on core.autocrlf=input to normalize intermediate content. The initial local tests inherited that user setting; hosted clean configurations did not.
